使用反流症状指数评估中国LPR筛查阴性患者SARS-CoV-2感染前及感染期间咽喉症状负担：一项前瞻性随访研究

Using the reflux symptom index to quantify throat symptom burden in LPR-screened-negative patients before and during SARS-CoV-2 infection in China: a prospective follow-up study.

中文摘要

本研究旨在使用反流症状指数（RSI）量化Omicron优势流行期间LPR筛查阴性患者SARS-CoV-2感染前及感染期间的咽喉症状负担，并识别感染期间与RSI评分升高独立相关的因素。 本前瞻性随访研究纳入2022年12月至2023年3月中国Omicron优势流行期间428例SARS-CoV-2感染的LPR筛查阴性参与者。在两个时间点进行RSI问卷调查：感染前基线和随访。第二份问卷在感染发病后≥4周完成，参与者回顾性回忆发病前2周内经历的急性症状。采用配对样本t检验、McNemar检验和多变量线性回归进行分析。 平均年龄为37.59±11.56岁；64.7%为女性。平均总RSI评分从基线的5.04±5.98显著升高至感染期间的9.68±7.48（平均ΔRSI=+4.64；p<0.001）。RSI>13的比例从9.1%上升至25.9%（p<0.001）。感染期间最常见的症状为烦人的咳嗽（79.2%）、清嗓（76.9%）和咽喉黏液过多（72.4%）。多变量线性回归识别出三个与RSI升高幅度更大独立相关的因素：鼻塞/流涕（β=3.30，95% CI 1.99-4.60，p<0.001）、乏力（β=2.53，95% CI 0.83-4.23，p=0.004）和肌肉疼痛（β=1.96，95% CI 0.59-3.32，p=0.005）。 Omicron优势流行期间的SARS-CoV-2感染显著加重了LPR筛查阴性患者的咽喉症状。同时出现乏力、鼻塞和肌肉疼痛的患者RSI升高幅度更大，可能需要更密切的临床关注。

英文摘要

This study aimed to quantify throat symptom burden using the Reflux Symptom Index (RSI) in laryngopharyngeal reflux (LPR)-screened-negative patients before and during SARS-CoV-2 infection in the Omicron-dominant period, and to identify factors independently associated with RSI score increase during infection. This prospective follow-up study enrolled 428 LPR-screened-negative participants with SARS-CoV-2 infection during the Omicron-dominant period (December 2022-March 2023) in China. RSI questionnaires were administered at two time points: pre-infection baseline and follow-up. The second questionnaire was completed ≥4 weeks after infection onset, and participants retrospectively recalled acute symptoms experienced during the first 2 weeks of illness. Paired-samples t-tests, McNemar's test, and multivariable linear regression were used for analysis. Mean age was 37.59 ± 11.56 years; 64.7% were female. Mean total RSI score increased significantly from 5.04 ± 5.98 at baseline to 9.68 ± 7.48 during infection (mean ΔRSI = +4.64; p < 0.001). The proportion with RSI > 13 rose from 9.1 to 25.9% (p < 0.001). The most common symptoms during infection were troublesome cough (79.2%), throat clearing (76.9%), and excess throat mucus (72.4%). Multivariable linear regression identified three factors independently associated with greater RSI increase: stuffy/runny nose (β = 3.30, 95% CI 1.99-4.60, p < 0.001), fatigue (β = 2.53, 95% CI 0.83-4.23, p = 0.004), and muscle pains (β = 1.96, 95% CI 0.59-3.32, p = 0.005). SARS-CoV-2 infection during the Omicron-dominant period significantly worsened throat symptoms in LPR-screened-negative patients. Patients presenting with concurrent fatigue, nasal congestion, and muscle pain showed higher RSI increases and may warrant closer clinical attention.
